title: ABA/1228/2024 of GIRI GAURAV NAITHANI ALIAS MUJIB NAITHANI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1228 of 2024
Giri Gaurav Naithani @ Mujib Naithani ...Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ....Respondent
 Present:-
Mr. Sanjay Bhatt and Mr. Prem Prakash Bhatt, Advocates for
the applicant.
Mr. V.S. Rawat, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. Mukesh Kaparuwan, Advocate for the informant.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant seeks anticipatory bail in Sessions
Trial No.23 of 2020, State Vs. Rajeev Gaur and Others, under
Section 307, 324, 384, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(s) of the
Schedule Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act, 1989, pending in the court of Sessions Judge,
Kotdwar, District Pauri Garhwal ("the Sessions Trial"), arising
out of FIR No.163 of 2020, Police Station Kotdwar, District
Pauri Garhwal.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. In the Sessions Trial, on 23.10.2020,
cognizance order was passed. It was challenged by the
applicant in C482 No.738 of 2020, Mujib Naithani alias Giri
Gaurav Naithani Vs. State and Another ("the Misc.
Application"). The Misc. Application was dismissed on
24.09.2024. The Court also passed the following order:-

2
"10. As the proceeding of the case is pending for a
long time, therefore, the petitioner/accused is directed
to appear before the court concerned on 01.10.2024 at
10:30 A.M. Trial Court is not required to issue notice of
appearance to the petitioner/accused."

4. On 01.10.2024, the applicant did not appear
before the court. He moved an application for exemption from
personal appearance. The court dismissed the exemption
application on the ground that the applicant did not appear
personally, as directed by this Court on 24.09.2024 in the
Misc. Application. The court below issued Non Bailable
Warrants against the applicant. The applicant still did not
appear. He did not move any application for recalling the
Non-Bailable Warrants on any time after its issuance.
Perusal of the order sheet passed in the case reveals that
even Non-Bailable Warrants could not be executed against
the applicant.
5. On 08.11.2024, the court noted that the
applicant is absconding and was not found for execution of
warrant. The court below allowed the application of the
Investigating Officer and issued processes under Section 82
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code"), against
the applicant and also issued Non-Bailable Warrants against
him.
6. It is in these factual circumstances, the
applicant seeks anticipatory bail.

3
7. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit
that after the order of this Court on 24.09.2024, the
applicant contacted his lawyer, who advised to move an
application for exemption from personal appearance. It is
argued that, in fact, the applicant wanted to challenge the
order dated 24.09.2024, of this Court passed in the Misc.
Application. Therefore, it is urged that the applicant may be
granted time to appear before the court.
8. The Misc. Application has already been rejected
by this Court on 24.09.2024. The applicant was directed by
this Court to appear before the court below on 01.10.2024, at
10:30 A.M. The applicant did not appear. He got an
application for exemption from personal appearance filed in
the court below, which was rejected by the court below on
the ground that the applicant defied the order of this Court
and did not appear personally. On that date, Non-Bailable
Warrants were issued against the applicant. Surprisingly, the
applicant did not appear before the court below after
01.10.2024 on any date. He did not move any application
even for recalling the Non-Bailable Warrants. His Non-Bailable Warrants could not be executed. The Investigating
Officer filed a report that the applicant is absconding. It is
under those circumstances that on 08.11.2024, the Court
had noted that since the applicant is absconding, processes

4
under Section 82 of the Code and Non-Bailable Warrants be
issued against him.
9. The applicant is repeatedly concealing his
presence, absconding, not appearing despite the orders of
this Court. Therefore, there is no reason to entertain this
anticipatory bail application. Accordingly, the instant
anticipatory bail application deserves to be dismissed.
10. The anticipatory bail application is dismissed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 10.12.2024
Ravi Bisht
